title: MCP OAuth: offer the RFC 8628 device authorization grant to MCP clients, so a client running on a remote or headless machine can be authorized from a phone without a localhost redirect
body:
repo:cloud#5 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPP1zuWBNq3nBXVei9

Filing gate: ③ a task on the maintainer's word, verbatim 「立卡」, given in the `repo:cloud#5` seat session (2026-11-20). He had just shown a remote MCP client failing to complete OAuth against a hosted environment. Reader: the `domain:server` lane (plugin-auth OAuth / MCP authorization). Dedupe: `device authorization MCP oauth` (is:issue) returned 5 unrelated QA-run and invitation cards; no open card covers this.

## 维护者速读
- 问题：MCP 客户端跑在云端电脑或服务器上（例如 WorkBuddy 的 Cloud Computer）时，用手机走 OAuth 授权，授权完会跳到 `http://localhost:<port>/callback`。这个地址指向手机自己，打不开，用户只能手动复制地址栏网址发回给客户端。
- 要做：MCP 的授权入口同时提供「设备码授权」（RFC 8628）。客户端显示一个短码，用户在手机上打开授权页、输入短码确认即可，不需要跳回 localhost。
- 平台已有这套机制：`objectstack login` 已经在用 `/api/v1/auth/device/code`。要补的是对 MCP 客户端开放，并在授权服务器元数据里声明它。
- 需要你做的：无。

## What was seen

A remote MCP client registered by DCR with a loopback redirect, `http://localhost:8765/callback`. That is allowed for native clients (RFC 8252; `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts` around lines 668–689). The user authorized from a phone. The redirect went to the phone's own localhost and failed. The flow only completed because the user copied the URL by hand back to the client.

## Measured (objectstack `main`)

- The device flow exists for the CLI: `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts` calls `POST /api/v1/auth/device/code` and polls with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`.
- The authorization-server metadata (`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts` around lines 6286–6292) is what MCP clients discover. Not yet read: whether it advertises `device_authorization_endpoint` and the device grant in `grant_types_supported`, and whether DCR accepts that grant for a public MCP client. The dev measures these first.

## Done when

- The MCP-facing authorization-server metadata advertises `device_authorization_endpoint`, and lists `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` in `grant_types_supported`.
- A DCR-registered public MCP client can complete the device flow and receive a token with the same scopes and consent screen as the authorization-code flow.
- The consent page names the client and the requested scopes before approval. The user code is short-lived and single-use.
- A test pins both the metadata and an end-to-end device-flow token for an MCP client.

The security reading is owed in the PR: user-code entropy and expiry, polling rate limits, and the consent page as the only approval point. Device-flow phishing (a code relayed to a victim) is mitigated by naming the client on consent.
